title: Error-Counter Defect with Unresolved Underlying Failure Rate
description: The user-service alert reports HTTP 5xx rate > 5%, with a displayed baseline of 0.5% and current rate of 8%. Code evidence establishes two increments per error, but the frozen evidence lacks aligned request totals, population coverage and numerator/denominator definitions. Only if those definitions and windows align does 8% / 2 imply 4%: eight times the 0.5% baseline, not normal; the reported 8% is sixteen times baseline. The scoring target is an evidence-bounded diagnosis of instrumentation error with unresolved underlying service health and alert validity, not a confirmed false positive or sole root cause.

Access logs report ~50 5xx/min unchanged, but no aligned total request counts are supplied

causal_chain.from_description: The deployed instrumentation revision adds a second increment for the same error event
causal_chain.to_description: The middleware and handler duplicate error-counter updates; this establishes a counter defect, not the dashboard rate denominator

causal_chain.from_description: The duplicate counter, log counts and successful trace sample do not supply comparable numerator/denominator populations
causal_chain.to_description: The displayed alert cannot establish whether a real rate increase coexists with instrumentation error or whether the alert is a false positive

ground_truth.insufficient_evidence_note: The scoring target is the unresolved underlying HTTP failure rate and alert validity. The code supports duplicate error-counter increments, but no aligned request denominator or complete population/window coverage is available. Conditional on identical rate definitions, denominator and window, 8% / 2 = 4%; 4% / 0.5% = 8 and 8% / 0.5% = 16. Thus even that conditional 4% is elevated relative to the supplied baseline, although below the stated >5% alert threshold. The ~50/min logs cannot supply a rate without total requests, and a successful sampled trace cannot exclude other failures. Do not infer a false-positive alert, normal service health, a confirmed real spike, or sole-cause attribution from these artifacts. High confidence in the code-level defect is not high confidence in the true rate.
contributing_factors: Duplicate error-counter updates in deployed instrumentation
Missing aligned rate definitions and request totals

must_not_claim: The actual error rate is normal
The alert is a confirmed false positive
The double increment is the sole incident root cause
The sampled logs or trace prove fleet-wide service health

misleading_or_confounding_signals: An unverified dashboard rate is not a validated request-failure rate
Stable error counts can coexist with changing request volume
Successful trace sampling does not rule out failures outside the sample

acceptable_alternatives.description: Identify the deployed counter defect while explicitly withholding judgment on the true failure rate, alert validity and any concurrent service fault

required_checks.description: Compare the reported metric and log error counts, checking denominator, population and window alignment before interpreting them as rates
required_checks.expected_outcome: The available logs provide an error count but not a comparable request denominator; neither an actual 4% rate nor normal health is established

required_checks.description: Review metrics middleware code for double increment
required_checks.expected_outcome: The error-counting path updates the same counter in both layers; that code review does not establish the dashboard denominator

required_checks.description: Request aligned error and total-request counts with the metric definition and sampling coverage
required_checks.expected_outcome: Aligned totals and numerator scope are absent from the frozen evidence; gathering them is necessary before confirming any underlying rate or false-positive diagnosis

remediation_guidance.suggestion: Propose fixing duplicate error-counter updates and validating rates against aligned request counts; continue investigating service health rather than dismissing the alert
test_plan: Unit-test one increment per error event
Verify numerator, denominator and sampling/window alignment
Reassess service health and the alert with validated rates; no recovery result is assumed
